name: Business Studies practice paper
subject: Business Studies

exam.title: Business Studies practice paper
exam.source: Marginal (original material written for regression coverage)

instructions: Attempt all questions. This paper is original material written to exercise the exam contract. It is not a past examination and its questions are not drawn from one.

sections.name: Section I - Multiple choice
sections.instructions: 10 marks. Attempt Questions 1 to 10. Allow about 15 minutes for this section.

questions.prompt: A bakery reduces the flour it throws away each week. Which operations performance objective is it pursuing?

choices.why: Reducing waste lowers the cost of inputs per unit produced, which is the cost objective.
Speed concerns how quickly an order moves through the process, not how much input is wasted.
Quality concerns whether the output meets its specification.
Flexibility concerns how readily the process changes what or how much it makes.

questions.prompt: A courier firm lets customers choose a delivery window. Which objective is this most directly serving?

choices.why: Offering a choice of windows means the process adapts to the customer, which is the flexibility objective.
Offering more choice usually raises cost rather than lowering it.
Quality is conformity to specification, not breadth of choice.
Dependability is keeping the promise once made, not offering the choice.

questions.prompt: Which of these appears on a balance sheet rather than a revenue statement?

choices.why: Accounts receivable is an asset held at a point in time, so it sits on the balance sheet.
Cost of goods sold measures activity over a period, so it belongs to the revenue statement.
Gross profit is a period result.
Sales revenue is a period flow.

questions.prompt: A business funds a new oven using retained profits. This is an example of:

choices.why: Retained profits are generated inside the business and are not repaid to a lender, so they are internal equity.
Debt finance is borrowed and repaid with interest.
External equity comes from new owners outside the business.
A financial institution is a source, not a type of finance.

questions.prompt: Which is a leading indicator of a firm's likely future labour needs?

choices.why: Planned openings tell a business what staffing it will need before the need arrives.
A past turnover rate describes what already happened.
Absenteeism describes the present position.
Historical costs describe the past.

questions.prompt: A firm's current ratio falls from 2.1 to 0.9 in one year. This most directly suggests a problem with:

choices.why: The current ratio compares current assets to current liabilities, which is the liquidity question.
Profitability is measured by return and margin ratios.
Efficiency is measured by turnover and expense ratios.
Solvency concerns long-term obligations rather than short-term ones.

questions.prompt: Which pricing method sets price by adding a percentage to unit cost?

choices.why: Cost-plus adds a fixed margin to the cost of producing each unit.
Market pricing sets price by what buyers and competitors will bear.
Competition-based pricing references rivals' prices.
A loss leader is priced below cost deliberately.

questions.prompt: A manufacturer moves production to a supplier overseas. This is:

choices.why: Contracting a process to an external provider in another country is global outsourcing.
A joint venture is a shared enterprise with another firm.
Franchising licenses a business format to an operator.
Vertical integration brings a stage of supply inside the firm rather than contracting it out.
Flexible hours have value to an employee without being a payment.
A bonus is a payment.
Share options are financial.
A salary increase is a payment.

questions.prompt: The main purpose of a cash flow statement is to show:

choices.t: Movements of cash in and out over a period
choices.why: It reports cash received and cash paid across the period.

choices.t: What the business owns and owes at a date
choices.why: That is the balance sheet.
That is the revenue statement, and profit is not the same as cash.

choices.t: The market value of the business
choices.why: No standard statement reports market value.

sections.name: Section II - Short answer
sections.instructions: 40 marks. Attempt Questions 11 to 13. Allow about 70 minutes for this section.

questions.instructions: Use the case study below when answering this question.

stimulus.caption: Case study: Kerbside Coffee
stimulus.text: Kerbside Coffee roasts and sells coffee from one site and four vans. Demand at the vans peaks between 7am and 9am, and the owners have had complaints about waiting times. Last year the business bought a second roaster using a three-year loan. Staff turnover among van operators is high, and most operators are employed casually.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Outline ONE operations performance objective Kerbside Coffee is failing to meet at its vans.
points: Names speed, or dependability, as the objective
Links it to the morning waiting times described in the case study

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Explain how the business's casual employment of van operators could be contributing to its turnover.
points: Explains that casual work carries no guaranteed hours or leave entitlements
Links that insecurity to an operator's decision to leave
Connects turnover to the cost of recruiting and training replacements

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Kerbside Coffee holds current assets of $60 000 and current liabilities of $40 000. Calculate its current ratio, correct to one decimal place.
parts.model: Current ratio = current assets divided by current liabilities = 60 000 / 40 000 = 1.5 to 1.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Justify ONE staffing strategy Kerbside Coffee could use to reduce waiting times at its vans during the morning peak.
points: Names a specific strategy, such as staggered shifts or a second operator on peak vans
Explains how the strategy shortens the queue at the times the case study identifies
Weighs the strategy against its wage cost
Reaches a supported judgement rather than listing options

questions.instructions: Use the data below when answering this question.

stimulus.caption: Table 1: Selected financial data, Harbourline Cycles
stimulus.text: 2024: sales $820 000, gross profit $328 000, expenses $250 000. 2025: sales $910 000, gross profit $337 000, expenses $301 000.

stimulus.caption: Note
stimulus.text: Harbourline Cycles imports its frames and assembles them locally. It has not changed its selling prices since 2024.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Describe what has happened to Harbourline Cycles' gross profit ratio between 2024 and 2025.
points: Identifies that the ratio has fallen
Refers to gross profit relative to sales rather than the dollar figure alone
Uses the data in Table 1 to support the statement

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Analyse TWO factors that could explain the change in the expense ratio shown in Table 1.
points: Identifies that expenses have risen faster than sales
Offers a first plausible cause and connects it to the figures
Offers a second plausible cause that is genuinely distinct from the first
Draws the two together rather than listing them

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Evaluate the usefulness of comparative ratio analysis for a business in Harbourline Cycles' position.
points: Explains what comparing ratios over time or against similar firms reveals
Identifies at least one genuine limitation, such as differences in accounting treatment
Applies the discussion to the importer's position described in the note
Reaches a judgement about usefulness rather than describing the technique

questions.prompt: Explain how TWO global factors can influence the operations of an Australian manufacturer.
points: Names a first global factor and explains its operational effect
Names a second, genuinely distinct global factor and explains its effect
Refers to operations processes rather than to the business in general
Uses an Australian manufacturing context

sections.name: Section III - Business report
sections.instructions: 20 marks. Attempt Question 14. Allow about 35 minutes for this section. Present your answer in the form of a business report.

questions.instructions: Use the case study below. Present your answer as a business report with a clear structure.

stimulus.caption: Case study: Tidewater Outfitters
stimulus.text: Tidewater Outfitters sells camping equipment through six stores and a website. Online sales have grown for three years while store sales have fallen. The business leases all six stores on agreements expiring within two years. Its warehouse was built for store replenishment and is now picking individual online orders, and delivery times have slipped. The owners want to keep all six stores.

questions.prompt: You have been engaged as a consultant to Tidewater Outfitters. Recommend strategies the business could use to respond to the shift in where its customers are buying.
points: Uses a report structure with headings rather than continuous prose
Identifies the operations problem created by a warehouse designed for a different job
Recommends at least two specific strategies rather than describing the situation
Addresses the owners' stated intention to keep all six stores
Justifies the recommendations against the evidence in the case study

sections.name: Section IV - Extended response
sections.instructions: 20 marks. Attempt EITHER Question 15 OR Question 16. Allow about 35 minutes for this section.

questions.label: Question 15
questions.prompt: Evaluate the effectiveness of marketing strategies in achieving the marketing objectives of a business you have studied.
questions.model: A strong response defines the marketing objectives it is judging against, selects strategies that genuinely serve those objectives, and reaches a sustained judgement supported by evidence from the business rather than a list of strategies in sequence.
points: States the marketing objectives being judged against
Selects strategies that serve those objectives rather than describing the marketing mix
Supports the judgement with evidence from a real business
Sustains one argument across the response rather than restarting each paragraph

questions.label: Question 16
questions.prompt: Evaluate the effectiveness of financial management strategies in achieving the financial objectives of a business you have studied.
questions.model: A strong response defines the financial objectives it is judging against, selects strategies that genuinely serve those objectives, and reaches a sustained judgement supported by evidence from the business rather than a list of strategies in sequence.
points: States the financial objectives being judged against
Selects strategies that serve those objectives rather than listing them
Supports the judgement with evidence from a real business
Sustains one argument across the response rather than restarting each paragraph
